title: Reversal equivalence for the two path-fiber orientations
statement:
Use simplicial sets, internal functor simplicial sets, Kan complexes and degreewise pullbacks of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Let $r:X\to Y$ be a simplicial map between Kan complexes in a common universe, and let $y\in Y$ be a vertex. Define
$$P_y=X\times_{r,Y,\operatorname{ev}_0}\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,Y)\times_{\operatorname{ev}_1,Y}\{y\},\qquad Q_y=\{y\}\times_{Y,\operatorname{ev}_0}\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,Y)\times_{\operatorname{ev}_1,Y,r}X.$$
Both are Kan complexes. There are simplicial maps $R:P_y\to Q_y$, $S:Q_y\to P_y$ commuting exactly with projection to $X$, and simplicial homotopies $SR\simeq\operatorname{id}_{P_y}$ and $RS\simeq\operatorname{id}_{Q_y}$ over $X$. A homotopy over $X$ means that its composite with the projection to $X$ is constant in the interval parameter. Homotopies have domain the product with $\Delta^1$; either endpoint orientation is permitted. No fibration assumption on $r$ and no nonemptiness assumption on $X$ is imposed.

source.place: Corollary 3.1.3.3 (Kerodon Tag 00TM), together with Corollary 3.1.3.6 and Example 3.1.8.10 on path fibrations. proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-kan-pullback-path-comparison] first to $U=X$, $V=\Delta^0$, $W=Y$, $u=r$, $v=y$, and then to $U=\Delta^0$, $V=X$, $u=y$, $v=r$. The displayed path pullbacks are precisely $P_y$ and $Q_y$ by their degreewise definitions in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], so both are Kan complexes. Only the unconditional Kan assertion is used; neither leg is assumed to be a fibration. The one-point simplicial set is Kan because any horn map into it has the unique extension.

source.place: Example 3.1.8.10 and Corollary 3.1.3.3 (00TM), path-pullback fibrancy; the existing path-pullback lemma supplies both orientations.

proof.text: Let $I=\Delta^1$, let $J=N(\mathcal J)$ and $i:I\hookrightarrow J$ be as in [lem-coef-walking-isomorphism-edge-anodyne], and put $A=\operatorname{Fun}(I,Y)$, $B=\operatorname{Fun}(J,Y)$, $q=i^*:B\to A$. For a boundary lifting problem of dimension $m\geq0$ for $q$, transposition of the defining internal-functor formula gives an extension problem into $Y$ from $(\partial\Delta^m\times J)\cup(\Delta^m\times I)$ to $\Delta^m\times J$. This inclusion is the pushout-product of the monomorphism $\partial\Delta^m\hookrightarrow\Delta^m$ and the anodyne map $i$. By [lem-coef-sset-anodyne-pushout-product] it has the left lifting property against $Y\to\Delta^0$, which is a Kan fibration since $Y$ is Kan. Thus the extension exists. Transposing back supplies the required boundary lift, including $m=0$. By [def-weil-pbc-trivial-kan-fibration], $q$ is a trivial Kan fibration.

source.place: Corollary 3.1.3.6, with Corollary 3.1.3.3 (00TM). Agent endpoint-reversal construction from the walking-isomorphism extension and relative lifting.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-trivial-kan-lifts-monomorphisms] to $q$ and the degreewise injection $\varnothing\hookrightarrow A$, with bottom map $1_A$. Choose a resulting simplicial section $\sigma:A\to B$, so $q\sigma=1_A$. The groupoid automorphism interchanging $0,1$ induces an involution $\tau:J\to J$. Write $\theta=\tau^*:B\to B$ and $t=q\theta:B\to A$. Put $T=t\sigma:A\to A$. Restriction to the two vertices gives the strict identities $\operatorname{ev}_0T=\operatorname{ev}_1$ and $\operatorname{ev}_1T=\operatorname{ev}_0$: indeed $\tau i$ has vertices $1,0$, and $q\sigma=1_A$ preserves both original endpoints. These are equalities of simplicial maps, hence hold for every parameter simplex.

source.place: Corollary 3.1.3.6, with Corollary 3.1.3.3 (00TM). Agent endpoint-reversal construction from the walking-isomorphism extension and relative lifting.

proof.text: The two maps $\sigma T,\theta\sigma:A\to B$ have the same composite with $q$, namely $T$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-trivial-kan-lifts-monomorphisms] to $q$ and the degreewise injection $A\times\partial I\hookrightarrow A\times I$, using these two maps on the endpoint summands and $T\operatorname{pr}_A$ on the bottom. This gives $H:A\times I\to B$ with $H|_0=\sigma T$, $H|_1=\theta\sigma$ and $qH=T\operatorname{pr}_A$. Put $h=tH$. Its endpoint maps are $T^2$ and $t\theta\sigma=q\theta^2\sigma=q\sigma=1_A$. For $e=0,1$, evaluation satisfies $\operatorname{ev}_e h=\operatorname{ev}_{1-e}qH=\operatorname{ev}_{1-e}T\operatorname{pr}_A=\operatorname{ev}_e\operatorname{pr}_A$. Thus this single simplicial homotopy from $T^2$ to the identity fixes both endpoints throughout, with no reversal of the homotopy interval.

source.place: Corollary 3.1.3.6, with Corollary 3.1.3.3 (00TM). Agent endpoint-reversal construction from the walking-isomorphism extension and relative lifting.

proof.text: Define $R(x,a)=(Ta,x)$ and $S(a,x)=(x,Ta)$ on the displayed pullbacks. The endpoint identities of Step 3 verify each pullback equation: $a:r(x)\to y$ goes to $Ta:y\to r(x)$, and conversely. These formulas commute with every simplicial operator because $T$ is simplicial, and both leave $x$ unchanged. They give $SR(x,a)=(x,T^2a)$ and $RS(a,x)=(T^2a,x)$. The formulas $(x,a,s)\mapsto(x,h(a,s))$ and $(a,x,s)\mapsto(h(a,s),x)$ therefore define the two required homotopies, by the endpoint equations of Step 4. Their composites with projection to $X$ are exactly the projection to $x$, independent of $s$. If $X$ or either pullback is empty, the same maps and homotopies restrict to the unique empty-domain maps. Every construction stays in the common universe.

source.place: Corollary 3.1.3.6, with Corollary 3.1.3.3 (00TM). Agent endpoint-reversal construction from the walking-isomorphism extension and relative lifting.
